Order 
This is an application for bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The petitioner is the 5th accused in Crime No.732 of 2012 of Museum Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram, who is alleged to have been committed offence punishable under Sections 273, 328 read with 34 IPC and Section 59(3) of the Food Safety and Standard Act 2006.

2. The allegation is that on 10.7.2012 accused 1 to 4 sold degraded food item known as 'Shavarma' to the defacto complainant and 10 others resulting in the death of one such person due to after effects of consuming food supplied by accused 1 to 4.
Allegation against the petitioner is that he had supplied putrified chicken which was cooked and served by hotels.
The petitioner was arrested on 19.7.2012 and since then he has been in custody.
The petitioner claim that he is totally innocent and he is falsely implicated in the case.
At any rate, it is pointed out that his continued custody is unnecessary.
3. The learned Public Prosecutor very vehemently opposed the application and releasing the petitioner now on bail.

4. After having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, it is seen that the only allegation against the petitioner is that he has supplied putrefied chicken which was cooked and supplied to the consumers by the hotels.

Since the petitioner has been in custody from 19.7.2012 onwards and his continued custody is unnecessary, the petition is allowed as follows:
1) The petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.10,000/-(Rupees Ten thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class-III,
Thiruvananthapuram.
2) The learned Magistrate shall ensure the identity of the sureties and veracity of the tax receipts produced by the sureties.
3)The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on every Wednesday between 10.00 A.M. And 11.00 A.M till final report is laid.
